seoTitle: Add a Video to Your eBay Listing from Your Phone
metaDescription: Learn how to record or upload a product video and add it to a new or existing eBay listing using your iPhone or mobile browser, including where it lands and how approval works.
intro: A single product video can do what a gallery of photos can't — show an item moving, spinning, or working the way it's supposed to, which matters most on used gear, collectibles, and anything where condition is hard to judge from a still image. eBay lets any seller attach a short video directly to a listing, but the upload lives inside the same Photos & Video panel you already use for pictures, and it behaves a little differently once it's in there. This guide walks through where to find it, what happens to the video's position once it's uploaded, and how long you should expect to wait before it actually shows up for buyers.

steps.heading: Sign in and open the listing you want to edit
steps.body: Whether you're starting a new listing or editing one that's already live, you'll get to the same Photos & Video panel — new listings show it during creation, existing ones show it when you click edit. On mobile this is the eBay app or your phone's browser; on desktop it's the same draft editor. Either way, sign in first, since the upload option only appears once you're authenticated on the account that owns (or will own) the listing.

steps.heading: Find the Photos & Video section
steps.body: Scroll to the Photos & Video block on the listing form. eBay spells out the limits right there: up to 24 photos and a one-minute video per listing. If you've already added photos, they'll fill the grid first, and the video upload sits alongside them as its own tile rather than a separate section — easy to miss the first time because it looks like just another photo slot until you look closely.

image.caption: The Photos & Video panel on a listing draft, with a tooltip warning that a video defaults to the second position and can't be rearranged.

steps.heading: Upload the video and note where it lands
steps.body: Tap the video tile and select your file. eBay is explicit about one quirk here: the video always defaults to the second position in the gallery, right after your main photo, and you can't drag it anywhere else. That's worth planning around before you upload — put your strongest, most representative photo in the first slot, since that's the one buyers see before the video even starts playing. Zoomed into the draft, the video sits in that second tile exactly as described, next to the main listing photo.

image.caption: A listing draft zoomed in, showing the video occupying the second tile in the gallery, immediately after the main photo.

steps.heading: Wait for eBay to review it
steps.body: Once uploaded, the video doesn't go live immediately. It shows a running timer and an "Under review" label directly on the thumbnail while eBay processes and checks it, and you can't publish it to buyers until that review clears. This step catches a lot of first-time uploaders off guard because the video appears to be sitting there doing nothing — it's genuinely just waiting on eBay's side, and there's no action needed from you beyond leaving it alone until the status changes.

image.caption: A newly uploaded video showing a running timer and an "Under review" badge while eBay processes it.

steps.heading: Know the format and length limits before you shoot
steps.body: eBay caps listing video at one minute, so plan your shot list around that rather than filming a long walkthrough and trying to trim it down later. A short, well-lit clip that shows the item from a few angles, demonstrates it powering on or functioning, and calls out any wear or damage will do more for buyer confidence than a longer video padded with filler. If your footage runs over the limit, trim it on your phone before uploading — eBay won't do that for you.

steps.heading: Troubleshoot a video that won't upload or appear
steps.body: If a video fails to attach, gets stuck in review far longer than expected, or doesn't show up after you've republished the listing, don't keep re-uploading the same file. Check that it's under the one-minute limit and in a common format like MP4 first, since most rejections trace back to one of those two things. If the file itself looks fine and it's still not resolving, eBay's help search is the fastest path to an actual answer rather than guessing — searching your exact symptom there surfaces the specific article for that failure mode instead of generic upload instructions.

steps.heading: Replace or remove the video later
steps.body: A video isn't permanent once it's attached — you can go back into the same Photos & Video panel at any time, delete the existing clip, and upload a new one if the item's condition changes or you find better footage. The replacement goes through the same review process as the original, so treat it as a fresh upload rather than an instant swap, and expect the same short wait before it's visible to buyers again.

faq.question: Can I add video to an existing eBay listing, not just a new one?
faq.answer: Yes. Open the listing in edit mode and the same Photos & Video panel with the video upload tile appears, whether the listing is brand new or already live.

faq.question: Where does the video show up in my listing's gallery?
faq.answer: eBay always places it in the second position, right after your main photo, and this can't be manually reordered — so choose your first photo carefully since it's what buyers see before the video.

faq.question: How long does it take for a video to appear on my listing?
faq.answer: There's an approval step after upload, shown as an "Under review" badge with a timer on the thumbnail. It's not instant, but no action is needed from you while it processes.

faq.question: What's the maximum length for an eBay listing video?
faq.answer: One minute. Trim your footage to fit before uploading, since eBay enforces the limit at the file level rather than cutting it for you.

faq.question: My video won't upload or is stuck reviewing — what should I check first?
faq.answer: Confirm it's under one minute and in a standard format like MP4, since those two issues cause most upload failures. If it still won't resolve, search eBay's help center for your exact symptom rather than re-uploading repeatedly.
